issues.legal_issue: A claimant’s substantially delayed challenge to an administrative decision may be denied relief for delay and laches.
material_facts: The Collector rejected the land application in 1999, and the revision challenging that decision was filed more than five years later.
The revisional authority rejected the revision for delay in 2005, but the respondent challenged that decision in the High Court only in 2011.
The respondent said it had recently learned of the revisional decision, but the Supreme Court agreed that it had remained indolent in pursuing its remedy.
The Supreme Court was hearing an appeal from a Division Bench decision that had reversed the Single Judge’s dismissal of the delayed challenge.
issues.conclusion: The Single Judge was right to deny indulgence because of the respondent’s delay and laches, and the Division Bench was not justified in reversing that decision.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle that a party who delays substantially in pursuing a remedy may be denied relief on grounds of delay and laches. It cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this principle.

rule.if: appeal_reviews_appellate_order_reversing_dismissal and writ_challenges_administrative_decision and challenge_filed_after_substantial_delay and no_adequate_explanation_for_delay

predicates.appeal_reviews_appellate_order_reversing: An appeal reviews an appellate order that reversed the dismissal of a claimant’s challenge.
predicates.writ_challenges_administrative_decision: A claimant brings a writ proceeding to challenge an administrative decision.
predicates.challenge_filed_after_substantial_delay: The claimant files the challenge after a substantial delay in pursuing the available remedy.
predicates.no_adequate_explanation_for_delay: The claimant does not provide an explanation that the court accepts as adequate for the delay.

issues.definition: When an appeal reviews an appellate reversal of a dismissed writ challenge, and the challenge was substantially delayed without an adequate explanation, the claimant is denied indulgence.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot direct allocation of alternative land where the application sought a specified parcel, the requested land is unavailable, and no entitlement to alternative land was established.
material_facts: The respondent’s application sought 1,500 acres in a specified survey area for salt production.
The application was rejected because the requested area was not available as a single parcel, and the State later stated that no land was available in the village.
The respondent argued that available land from other survey areas should be allotted instead.
The policy said to support that entitlement had not been referred to or relied on in the earlier proceedings, and no submission had previously been made about entitlement under it.
The Division Bench directed the Collector to allot land from any survey area, and the Supreme Court held that direction unjustified.
issues.conclusion: The Division Bench was not right to direct the Collector to allot land for salt production from another survey area.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held, on the circumstances of the application and record, that the requested allotment did not justify a direction to provide land from other survey areas where no entitlement to that alternative had been established and the State’s position was that no land was available. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.

predicates.appeal_reviews_order_directing_land_allo: An appeal reviews an order directing a public authority to allocate land.
predicates.application_sought_specified_land: The applicant’s land application sought a specified parcel or area for a stated use.
predicates.requested_land_unavailable: The public authority states, and the court accepts on the record, that the requested land is unavailable.
predicates.alternative_land_entitlement_not_establi: The applicant did not establish an entitlement to land from other areas in the proceedings before the direction was made.

issues.definition: When an appeal reviews a land-allocation direction, the application sought specified land that is unavailable, and no entitlement to alternative land was established, mandatory allocation of alternative land is unjustified.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot rely after the hearing on a policy that was not raised or relied on during the proceedings to establish an entitlement that was never previously advanced.
material_facts: After the hearing had concluded, the respondent applied for directions seeking to rely on a government policy.
The policy had not been referred to or relied on at any earlier stage, and no earlier submission had addressed the respondent’s entitlement under it.
The Supreme Court rejected the application for directions.
issues.conclusion: The application for directions was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to entertain reliance on material introduced after the hearing where that material had not previously been raised or relied on and no earlier submission had established the claimed entitlement. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited.

predicates.application_made_after_conclusion_of_hea: A party makes an application after the court has concluded hearing the matter.
predicates.seeks_to_rely_on_policy_not_previously_r: The application seeks to rely on a policy that was not previously referred to or relied on in the proceedings.
predicates.no_prior_submission_established_entitlem: No submission made before the hearing concluded established the party’s claimed entitlement under that policy.

issues.definition: When a party applies after the hearing to rely on a previously unraised policy and no earlier submission established the claimed entitlement, the post-hearing application is rejected.
